intent: Artifact-only adversarial review of a DECISION or analysis. The reviewer must NOT gather evidence; it reasons solely on an inline ARTIFACT + CONTRACT and emits a machine-readable verdict plus a Claims-To-Verify handoff.

toolAccess.rationale: An artifact-only critic that can read files, run shells/evals, or call MCP tools can — and historically did — gather evidence, misread it, and assert a fabricated fact as a finding. An empty allow-list makes evidence-gathering, and therefore fabrication, STRUCTURALLY impossible rather than merely discouraged by prose.

enforcement.note: An adapter MUST emit at the highest level its host supports and MUST warn if the host cannot reach minimumLevel. Below L1, the no-tools contract is advice the model can violate, so the structural guarantee is lost.

L0.name: prompt-only
L0.guarantee: None enforced. The 'you have no tools' contract lives only in the prompt; if the host grants tools, the model can still call them. Fabrication is discouraged, not prevented.
L0.useWhen: The host cannot restrict tools per-agent at all.

L1.name: denylist
L1.guarantee: Named evidence/mutation tools are removed. Blocks the PRIMARY fabrication path (read-a-log, run-an-eval, write-a-file). Residual leak possible for any tool the denylist cannot name (e.g. dynamically-registered MCP tools when the denylist has no wildcard).
L1.useWhen: The host supports a per-agent denylist but not an allow-list, or as a belt-and-suspenders fallback beneath L2.

L2.name: empty-allowlist
L2.guarantee: The agent resolves to ZERO tools — core and MCP. Evidence-gathering is structurally impossible. This is the target level.
L2.useWhen: The host supports a per-agent allow-list (allow-lists typically exclude inherited MCP tools, which a denylist cannot).

output.note: Hosts that support structured/tool-forced output should validate against output.schema.json so the orchestrator can machine-read claimsToVerify. Hosts without it fall back to the labeled-prose fields named in prompt.md.
